info.text:
In the year to August 2026, average hourly pay rose 3.1% while consumer prices rose 3.4%, so real hourly pay fell 0.3%. This video explains inflation from zero: how the BLS measures it with the CPI, why the Fed aims for 2%, the four big causes (demand, costs, money and expectations), and 50 years of history from the 1970s and Paul Volcker to the 9.1% peak in June 2022 and the Fed's September 2026 hike. It works through a hypothetical $10,000 savings example with exact math, the rule of 72, and how I bonds, TIPS, fixed-rate debt and Social Security's COLA handle inflation.

Sources: BLS Consumer Price Index and Real Earnings releases for August 2026 (Sep 11, 2026) and June 2022 (Jul 13, 2022); BLS CPI-U annual averages; Federal Reserve, Statement on Longer-Run Goals (Jan 2012); Federal Reserve History, Volcker's anti-inflation measures; Reuters and Trading Economics (Sep 2026); Atlanta Fed (May 2021) on M2; TreasuryDirect I bond rate release (May 1, 2026) and TIPS page; SSA COLA announcement (Oct 2025); FDIC national rates (Aug 2026); Milton Friedman (1963).

News and education, not financial advice.

#inflation #personalfinance #ibonds
